claims.evidence: Witness only read an embossed 'POWER' logo on the front panel; no 'HP' branding or 'lunch bag' designation was mentioned. Could be a mismatched or copy-pasted title.

claims.claim: Like new, never repaired or opened
claims.evidence: Interior condition, lining, and signs of repair are not visible in the reported photo.
A bag has no mechanism to 'work'; this phrase is unverifiable and suggests boilerplate text possibly reused from an electronics listing.
No receipt, warranty card, or proof-of-purchase document was seen in the photo.

risks.proof: Close-up video or photo of zippers opening/closing and interior lining
risks.if_unproven: priced as if zippers may be faulty

risks.risk: Stains, tears, or odors inside the bag
risks.proof: Clear interior photo under good light
Close-up of fabric/material label or texture shot
risks.if_unproven: priced as generic/unknown material, not premium

risks.risk: Mismatch between seller's 'HP Power lunch bag' title and witness-observed 'POWER' logo small bag, possibly a template or wrong listing
risks.proof: Photo showing full brand tag/label and a shot matching the exact listing title

risks.risk: Shoulder strap or accessories claimed vs included
risks.proof: Photo showing all included accessories together
risks.if_unproven: priced as bag only, no extras

proof_requests: Clear photo of any brand label/tag inside or outside the bag
Interior photo showing lining condition and any stains/tears
Video of zippers and pockets opening and closing
Photo of the original receipt and warranty card if available
Photo showing all accessories (straps, dust bag, etc.) included in the sale
response.reason: The witness clearly identifies a small bag with a 'POWER' logo, so it can be priced at worst case for an unbranded, unverified-condition bag; the seller's electronics-style claims ('works perfectly', 'HP') are unverifiable and treated as unproven rather than fraud outright.
